title: Transfer: Largest Island Area
oneLiner: Same 0/1 map as Number of Islands, changed question: how many cells does the biggest island have? Make the flood fill count what it sinks.
keyTakeaway: Changing "how many components" to "how big is the biggest" changes only what the flood fill returns: it counts the cells it marks, and the outer scan keeps the maximum. The visited marking, the bounds checks and the O(rows x cols) cost are unchanged.
explanation:
This follows Number of Islands with the requirement changed. The grid is the same (1 is land, 0 is water, and land cells joined up, down, left or right form one island), but now return the area of the largest island, the number of cells in it, or 0 if there is no land at all.

The outer scan stays: visit every cell, and when you find land nobody has marked yet, you have found a new island. What changes is the flood fill. Instead of only marking cells, it counts them: start a counter at 0, and each time you pop (or recurse into) a land cell, mark it and add 1. When the fill finishes, the counter is that island's area. Compare it with the best so far.

Mark a cell as visited when you push it, not when you pop it. If you only mark at pop time, a cell reachable from two neighbours is pushed twice, and unless you also skip already marked cells when you pop them it is counted twice, so the area comes out too big. That bug is invisible in Number of Islands, where the number of islands is the same either way, which is why this changed requirement is worth doing.

The cost is still O(rows x cols): each cell is scanned once and filled at most once. An explicit stack avoids deep recursion on a big all-land grid.

The visualization fills each island of a small map and shows its area as it finishes.

Explain why the same idea works: before you move on, write two or three sentences on what you changed from Number of Islands and what you did not. Why is the scan plus flood fill still enough to find every island exactly once, and why does marking at push time matter now when it did not for counting islands?

visualizationSteps.message: Same scan as Number of Islands. This time each flood fill counts the cells it marks, and the tracker keeps the largest count.
New land at (0, 0). The flood fill marks 3 cells, so this island's area is 3. That beats 0: largest is now 3.
New land at (0, 4). The flood fill marks 5 cells, so this island's area is 5. That beats 3: largest is now 5.
New land at (3, 0). The flood fill marks 1 cell, so this island's area is 1. Not more than 5, so the largest stays 5.
Every cell scanned, every island filled once. Largest area: 5. Only the return value of the flood fill changed from Number of Islands.

recognitionSignals: A grid of cells where same kind neighbours form regions, and you need a size, perimeter or other total per region.
"Largest", "biggest" or "area of" a connected blob of cells.
gotchas: Mark cells when they are pushed; marking only when popped lets a cell reachable two ways be counted twice.
A grid with no land returns 0, not the area of an empty island or -1.
Diagonal cells are not neighbours: [[1, 0], [0, 1]] has two islands of area 1.
confusableWith: Grid Flood Fill: Number of Islands counts how many fills start; this one keeps the largest fill size. Same traversal, different thing returned.

complexity.note: Every cell is scanned once and pushed onto a flood-fill stack at most once. The stack can hold most of the grid when it is all land.
